messages:
Incident Bot: automatic page triggered — elevated 5xx + timeouts on /v1/generate in us-west-2
Jordan (oncall): got the page, pulling up dashboards now. seeing a p99 spike to ~4.8s and p95 to 1.6s, errors ~3.2% over baseline :grimacing:
Alex R: recent deploy landed 1798543000 ~ 6m ago. rolling canary -> global cutover at 1798543070. could be that change.
Maya T: I’m on traces. majority of timeouts originate from runtime-proxy -> model-gateway path, TLS connection timeouts and a couple 502s.
Sanjay P: Looking at routing: a subset of requests are getting routed to a new kernel variant (q4_0) — early suspicion: kernel path regression.
Jordan (oncall): status check: are customer-facing APIs impacted? support reports uptick in tickets.
Support Pager: confirmed, a handful of high-traffic customers reporting timeouts and partial failures. Severity: P2 escalating to P1 if persists.
Evelyn (eng-runtime): I can yank the kernel flag from traffic for new requests. can we fallback to previous model variant while we investigate?
Alex R: +1 fallback. if we can route by model-variant label that’s fastest. Jordan do you want to trigger rollback?
Jordan (oncall): yes. initiate immediate rollback of the cutover. Deploy Bot, start rollback to 1798539900 (pre-change).
Deploy Bot: rollback job queued -> gradelog id=rl-1798543210. Rolling back canary then global. ETA ~90s per cohort.
Maya T: putting a short diagnostic curl to reproduce locally:

```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

seeing `upstream timed out` and intermittent `502 Bad Gateway` in response headers.
Sanjay P: checking connection pool metrics — we see a spike in `conn_wait` and `connect_timeout` for instances with q4_0 kernel.
Evelyn (eng-runtime): rollback confirmed: canary cohort reverted at 1798543244. global rollbacks in progress. traffic shifting back to stable variant.
Jordan (oncall): good. start customer comms draft for affected customers. Maya can you capture before/after SLO numbers for support and post in thread?
Maya T: copying charts: pre-deploy p99 ~0.45s, p95 ~0.12s, error rate 0.15%. post-deploy peaked p99 4.8s, p95 1.6s, errors 3.2%. after rollback p99 down to 0.5s and errors dropping toward 0.2%.
Alex R: thanks. does telemetry show any KV cache evictions or cold-starts that co-occurred with the deploy?
Sanjay P: KV cache evictions were slightly higher but only on the q4_0 hosts. looks like memory pressure from the new kernel variant causing slower responses and connection churn.
Jordan (oncall): any customer data exfil risk? security check.
Evelyn (eng-runtime): negative — failures are timeouts/5xx only. no anomalous KMS or data plane access.
Support Pager: sending update to customers: "We observed elevated 5xx/timeouts affecting a subset of requests around 21:00 UTC after a recent change. We rolled back the change and are monitoring. Full postmortem to follow." :email:
Maya T: Metrics now stabilizing. p95 ~0.13s, p99 ~0.6s, errors ~0.25%. continuing to observe for 10m before close.
Alex R: follow-up items: (1) block q4_0 kernel rollout until further validation, (2) add canary perf gates for conn_wait/connect_timeout, (3) add automatic rollback threshold at error_rate >1%.
Jordan (oncall): I’ll file the incident and assign owners. handing off to SRE team for postmortem and followups. tagging @Evelyn and @Sanjay to lead.
Sanjay P: noted. will collect flamegraphs and kernel telemetry. ETA initial triage doc in 2 hours.
Evelyn (eng-runtime): I’ll prepare the rollback postmortem with rollout timeline and mitigation knobs. also add a script to force-avoid kernel variant by label during emergency.
Incident Bot: incident resolved -> status transitioning to monitoring. incident-id: INC-1798543210
Jordan (oncall): thanks all. if we see any regression alerts re-open. closing thread after 15m of stable telemetry.
Support Pager: posted customer note and queued follow-up for engineering update in 24h.
Maya T: last check 1798543287: telemetry stable. closing monitoring window in progress. :white_check_mark:
